evals.prompt: address the review comments on PR 285, don't resolve anything yet
evals.expected_output: Fetches open threads via pr.py threads, verifies each against current HEAD, fixes what verifies, drafts a reply per thread with --dry-run, and ends by asking whether to post and whether to commit. Posts in one --batch call, no entry with "resolve": true, only after a yes.
assertions: scripts/pr.py threads ran before any reply
Every finding carries a label of Reproduced, Traced, Unverified, or Refuted before being replied to
No reply was posted before the user said to post
No thread was resolved (no entry set "resolve": true)
The report's first line is verdict-first, e.g. 'N threads: ...'
The report asks whether to post and whether to commit, and neither happened without a yes
On 'post' with fixes not yet pushed, the agent asked whether to commit and push first instead of posting

evals.prompt: handle the open threads on !482, resolve the ones you fix
evals.expected_output: GitLab discussions fetched with full note history (not just the first note). Replies are drafted, then posted on the user's yes; fixed findings get "resolve": true in the batch, refuted or skipped ones stay open.
assertions: scripts/pr.py threads returned all notes per discussion, not just the first
Only threads whose finding was fixed had "resolve": true in the batch
A refuted thread got a reply explaining why, without "resolve": true
No commit was made without asking first

evals.prompt: deal with the comments on PR 12, but ignore the one about duplicated code
evals.expected_output: The duplicated-code thread is excluded before verification and reported as 'Skipped (user excluded)', spending no verification effort on it; the rest go through the normal extract-verify-apply-reply flow.
assertions: The excluded thread was never sent to the verifier
The report lists it under a 'Skipped (user excluded)' line, not as verified-then-dropped
Other threads were verified and replied to normally

evals.prompt: respond to the comments on this PR, one of them cites a rule from AGENTS.md that I don't think exists
evals.expected_output: The fabricated-rule thread comes back Refuted with evidence that the cited text was not found via grep and git log, and is reported, not silently dropped.
assertions: The thread with the fabricated rule is labeled Refuted
The evidence cites a grep or git log search that found no such rule
A reply explaining the refutation was drafted for that thread, and posted on the user's yes
The thread appears in the final report, not silently dropped

evals.prompt: address the comments on PR 9, it's already merged
evals.expected_output: pr.py reply refuses with exit 4 until the user explicitly says to reply anyway with --allow-closed; nothing is replied to or resolved without that.
assertions: No reply was posted before the user was told the PR is merged and asked how to proceed
reply was only retried with --allow-closed after an explicit yes
No thread was resolved without the user separately asking to resolve
